newsitem.title: GERMANY: WestLB's Neuger critical of recent tax probe.
newsitem.headline: WestLB's Neuger critical of recent tax probe.

text.p: Management board chairman of Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale, Friedel Neuber was critical of the recent probe by German tax authorities probe into suspected tax-evasion at branches of WestLB.
"Banks can only tell a customer what their particular tax requirements are, not improve the customer's behaviour when it comes to fulfilling those requirements," Neuber said.

German tax authorities investigated a number of WestLB branches and other savings banks on suspicion that WestLB employees helped customers in evading taxes, with suspicions of illegal transfers of funds to Luxembourg and Switzerland.
Neuber said that the bank had told its employees in 1992 and 1993 that customers should be made aware that interest income from Luxembourg and Switzerland was also liable for German income tax.
Employees had been told that any consultation with the customer should be broken off, if a customer seemed not to be complying with the law, said Neuber.
Neuber said he hoped the investigation by the tax authorities would be concluded soon, so that WestLB could examine the results in detail.
